subject: general
question: Manisha bought a toy for ₹849, decorated it at a cost of ₹6 and sold the toy for ₹441. Find the loss or profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost Price (CP) = 849 + 6 = 855.

Selling Price (SP) = 441.

Since SP [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Purchase Price = 849, Decoration Cost = 6, Selling Price (SP) = 441.

**Formulas:** Total CP = Purchase Price + Overhead Expenses | Loss = CP − SP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a067b504d0061b3b9d88f2111af5272f4502f9fa27e706be3cf51be7b7e9a529.png] 

⇒ Total **Cost Price (CP)** = 849 + 6 = **855**.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = **441**.

⇒ **Loss** = 855 − 441 = **414**.

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (414 ÷ 855) × 100.

⇒ Dividing both 414 and 855 by 9: (46 ÷ 95) × 100.

⇒ Dividing by 5: 46 × (20 ÷ 19) = **920/19%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 920/19% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Cost Price

Total CP includes the **buying price** plus all **overhead expenses** like repairs, decoration, or transportation.

Profit and Loss Condition

If **SP > CP**, it results in a **Profit**. If **CP > SP**, it results in a **Loss**.</p
